Use this page to find material that teaches what this guide assumes or only
touches on: R itself, epidemiological methods and statistics. If you only pick
one, start with the [DDEA (Danish Diabetes and Endocrine Academy) introductory
course](https://r-cubed-intro.rostools.org/) if you are completely new to R, or
[The Epidemiologist R Handbook](https://www.epirhandbook.com/en/) if you know a
bit of R and want to go straight to health science applications.

## Getting started - learn R

  | Resource                                                         | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
  | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | [DDEA introductory course](https://r-cubed-intro.rostools.org/)  | A 3-day workshop on reproducible data analysis with R, RStudio, Quarto and Git, run several times by the Danish Diabetes and Endocrine Academy (DDEA). The material is free to use (CC BY 4.0). Best starting point if you are completely new.                               |
  | [R for Data Science](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/)                    | Free e-book by Hadley Wickham, Mine Çetinkaya-Rundel and Garrett Grolemund (2nd edition) - the standard reference for modern R with the tidyverse. Concept-based, read from start to finish.                                                                                  |
  | [Cookbook for R](http://www.cookbook-r.com)                      | Task-based reference: "how do I do X?" with direct code examples. Strongest for its ggplot2 graphics recipes (legends, faceting, colours). Note: parts of the base-R and data-handling sections predate the tidyverse, so the syntax can differ from the rest of this guide. |
  | [Quick-R](https://www.statmethods.net)                           | Compact reference for R syntax and statistics, good for quick lookups mid-script. The address now redirects to DataCamp, which hosts the pages.                                                                                                                               |

## Health science and epidemiology

  | Resource                                                                      | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
  | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | [The Epidemiologist R Handbook](https://www.epirhandbook.com/en/)             | Practical reference written for epidemiologists and health researchers - covers data cleaning, analyses and visualisation with health science examples. Most relevant chapters for register work: dates, joins, data cleaning, regression and survival analysis. Most pages in this guide link to the matching chapter. |
  | [Zheer's R Coding Café](https://r-coding-cafe.zheer.dk/)                      | A bi-weekly open coding café, each session starting with a short presentation, for people working at Steno Diabetes Center Aarhus and several Aarhus University departments.                                                                                                                                            |
  | [CRAN (the Comprehensive R Archive Network, where R packages are published) Task View: Epidemiology](https://cran.r-project.org/view=Epidemiology)  | Package list for epidemiology - incidence rates, matching, cohort analysis. Good starting point when looking for the right package.                                                                                                                                                                                     |
  | [CRAN Task View: Survival Analysis](https://cran.r-project.org/view=Survival) | Package list for survival analysis - Cox regression, Kaplan–Meier and competing risks.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

**Podcasts:**

  | Resource                                                                   | What it is                                                                                                                                  |
  | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | [SERious Epi](https://seriousepi.blubrry.net/)                             | Podcast from the Society for Epidemiologic Research on epidemiological methods: study design, confounding, selection bias, measurement error. |
  | [Casual Inference](https://open.spotify.com/show/1L8TqB17Peo7jNgXuPObwi)   | Podcast on causal inference and statistics, in an informal conversational format.                                                           |

## Methods and statistics

  | Resource                                                                                         | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
  | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | [Learning Statistics with R](https://learningstatisticswithr.com/)                               | Free e-book by Danielle Navarro - covers statistical theory and R implementation side by side, from basic probability to regression and ANOVA. Written for a non-mathematical audience. Relevant if you want to understand the statistics you are running, not just copy the code. |
  | [Causal Inference: What If (Hernán & Robins)](https://miguelhernan.org/whatifbook)               | Free PDF - the standard reference on causal inference, confounding and DAGs (directed acyclic graphs). Epidemiological methods, not R.                                                                                                                                                                       |
  | [Analysis of mechanisms (mediation analysis course)](https://analysis-of-mechanisms.netlify.app) | A 3-day course on modern mediation analysis for PhD students and postdocs in diabetes and endocrinology, sponsored by the DDEA. Use it when you need to decompose an effect into direct and indirect (mediated) paths. General method, not register-specific.                       |
